subject: keen-code
title: TurnMemory: future-turn history carries placement-tagged tool ACTIVITY records, not results - raw outputs are json:"-" excluded and survive only in-session under /tool-history full
one_why: A fourth state layer between the provider-native active loop and the session transcript: cross-turn projection keeps 'what ran, where in the prose, did it succeed' and drops stale contents by default, with a user-visible opt-in for full retention - closest cousin is memcode's thrash-aware-tool-eviction (reactive dedup) but this is a structural projection layer, not an eviction policy

subject: keen-code
title: Ephemeral breakpoints at stable-prefix end AND last message, and mode switches never change the tool-definition prefix: plan-mode denial wraps tools instead of removing them
one_why: The denyWriteToolRegistry trick keeps tool definitions byte-stable across build/plan mode toggles purely to preserve cache hits - most subjects re-send a changed tool list on mode switch and silently bust the cache

subject: keen-code
title: Auto-compact trigger estimates tokens of the ACTUAL serialized outgoing request (json.Marshal of provider params) at 90% of input budget, mid-tool-loop, and the compaction call is user-cancellable mid-flight
one_why: Nuance on zot's measured-input trigger: keen re-serializes the pending request per loop iteration rather than reusing last-turn reported usage, and exposes a Cancel handle on the AutoCompactionEvent so a runaway summarize is interruptable; replacement is transactional (empty-summary and incomplete-stream rejected, tested at auto_compaction_test.go:63,90)

subject: keen-code
title: Each connected MCP server auto-generates a managed skill (mcp:<server>) containing a tool table; full JSON schemas load on demand - no tool-search-tool needed
one_why: Converges with crab-code's prompt-to-skill conversion and the lazy-tool-catalog intent (forge-norvialabs), but keen's unit is the whole server's TOOL catalog expressed as ordinary skill docs, reusing the skills loader rather than adding a catalog mechanism

subject: keen-code
title: Guard: system-path denylist + blanket block of every $HOME dotfile + gitignored paths, with per-agent artifact allow-dirs that explicitly reject symlinks via Lstat
one_why: Component-safe prefix checks on cleaned absolute paths (no sibling-prefix escape like claii's), and the IsInKeenBashDir/MCPArtifactsDir/WebFetchArtifactsDir allow-dirs refuse to trust paths whose final component is a symlink - a small hardening most prefix-based guards skip

subject: keen-code
title: Five-step approval ladder (yolo -> headless autoApprove -> project allow -> session allow -> prompt) where 'allow session' deliberately never sticks to dangerous commands, but the project allow-list can skip even the dangerous-bash prompt
one_why: The session-scope anti-sticky rule for dangerous actions is a good least-privilege default; its mirror is the foot-gun: allow:["bash"] in .keen/permissions.json also mutes the danger prompt - documented honestly in permission-system.md, which itself earns the honesty credit

subject: keen-code
title: /adversary: user-launched second-model reviewer on a SEPARATE provider client whose tool registry is stripped of write_file/edit_file/bash/call_mcp_tool/delegate_task
one_why: No pool/prewarm (contrast codex guardian_review.rs) - on-demand instead - but the enforcement is registry intersection, so the reviewer physically cannot mutate anything regardless of what its model decides

subject: keen-code
title: /btw side-question runs a tool-less one-shot over a last-10-message window alongside the main stream, bypassing the 5-item input queue
one_why: Same shape as kimi-code's btw feature - convergent design; keen's nuance is the bounded history slice (btwContext trims the trailing user msg, keeps 10) so side questions never serialize behind busy turns or pollute main history

subject: keen-code
title: The tool-loop scaffold (maxToolTurns loop, proactive-compaction hook, incomplete-exit, pending-state injection) is re-implemented in all six provider clients
evidence: internal/llm/anthropic.go:673; bedrock.go:277; openai.go:516; genkit.go:26; openai_responses.go:214; openai_codex.go:81
one_why: tool_execution.go, auto_compaction.go and the compaction package prove the shared seam exists, yet each client copies the control flow around it - six places to fix any loop-semantics bug; protocol differences justify provider encoding, not loop duplication

subject: keen-code
title: Dangerous-bash classifier is segment- and subshell-aware (splits pipelines, extracts $(...), flags privilege escalation and secret-exposure env reads like cat $AWS_SECRET) rather than a flat regex list
one_why: Stronger convergent variant of the regex-denylist family (nanocoder, bash-ast-rule-matching subjects), including a secret-exposure dimension few denylists have - still fundamentally bypassable (find -delete, interpreter-mediated writes) and should be read as prompt-elevation for the approval UI, not enforcement

subject: keen-code
title: GA4 session start/end telemetry is on by default at build time, with opt-out only via KEEN_TELEMETRY / DO_NOT_TRACK / CI env vars
one_why: Payload is minimal (session start/end, version, OS, random client ID persisted in ~/.keen/state.json) and honors DO_NOT_TRACK, but a solo OSS coding agent phoning home by default is still a posture note users should find themselves
